Estimate a reduced-form VAR by least squares

Source: R/varm.R
varm.Rd

Equation-by-equation OLS (identical to Gaussian ML for the coefficients) of $$y_t = c + \sum_{l=1}^p A_l y_{t-l} + \Gamma w_t + u_t,\quad u_t \sim (0,\Sigma).$$ The estimation loop is compiled (RcppArmadillo).

Usage

varm(Y, p = 1L, const = TRUE, trend = FALSE, exog = NULL, vars = NULL)

Arguments

Y

data frame (preferred), ts or numeric matrix (T x K) of endogenous variables. Non-numeric columns of a data frame are dropped; a Date column is kept as $dates and used by the plots.

p

lag order.

const

include a constant.

trend

include a linear trend.

exog

optional T x q matrix or data frame of exogenous regressors (contemporaneous, treated like deterministic terms; future values are then required for forecasting).

vars

<tidy-select> columns of Y that are the endogenous variables, e.g. vars = c(infl, rate). Default: all numeric columns.

Value

an object of class varm with elements B (m x K coefficient matrix, lags first then deterministics), Sigma (degrees-of-freedom corrected), U residuals, XtXinv, logLik and metadata. See tidy.varm(), glance.varm() and augment.varm() for tibble summaries.

Details

See vignette("var-theory") for definitions and the economic reading of the estimates.

See also

Other estimation: lag_matrices(), stability(), var_select()

Examples

fit <- varm(yraw, p = 2)
fit
#> <varm> VAR(2) with 3 variables, 213 effective observations
#> logLik = -338.416; max |eigenvalue| = 0.946
#> 
#>             infl   unemp    rate
#> infl.l1   1.5378 -0.0095  0.5457
#> unemp.l1 -0.2809  1.3297 -0.6475
#> rate.l1  -0.0571 -0.0210  0.7766
#> infl.l2  -0.5418  0.0341 -0.4395
#> unemp.l2  0.2336 -0.4290  0.6730
#> rate.l2   0.0580  0.0457  0.1232
#> const     0.2872  0.3654  0.0052
summary(fit)
